description:
Describe Changes in System Dynamics Before, During and After a Minibang

A minibang is a temporal event in which the dynamics of the whole system changes qualitatively over a relatively short interval. It can simplify or enrich the dynamics. Interpret the dynamics through a biological-population intuition: distinguish species-like types of organisms and examine their behavior, interactions and collective organization. A qualitative change alters the system's repertoire of persistent types, their number or role, or the sustained way those populations move, interact or organize. This is an interpretive analogy, not a claim of real biological taxonomy or living organisms. Rendered color and total mass alone do not identify a type or determine whether its dynamics changed. The initial explosion and settling are outside the task: observations are available only from the human-annotated onset of established dynamics onward. Color change alone, a reversible fluctuation, or an isolated object's motion is insufficient. RGB shows only part of the state: object identity is not identical to rendered color. Time is in raw simulation steps; 3000 steps correspond to one video second. Intervals are half-open [start, end). The event start is the last moment of the previous established dynamics; the event end is the first moment of the next established dynamics. Established dynamics can include persistent motion and fluctuations: established does not mean motionless.

In this description task, identity means a coherent visual or morphodynamic phenotype, not material continuity or an individual particle lineage. Distinguish individual coherent organisms from their visible parts and from species-like populations. Dynamics includes deformation as well as locomotion; follow any explicit specification that distinguishes shape change from translation. Persistent or ongoing activity describes a recurring established regime, unless the statement explicitly requires uninterrupted continuity or a quantitative condition. Preserve explicit numeric rates, comparisons, phase distinctions and the distinction between an organism body and a surrounding field.
